# LogSlider { #anylumino.astryx.LogSlider }

```python
LogSlider(
    value=1,
    *,
    label='',
    base=10,
    min_exponent=0,
    max_exponent=4,
    step=0.1,
    disabled=False,
    value_display=None,
    description=None,
    **props,
)
```

Render an Astryx slider on a logarithmic scale.

Astryx ``Slider`` steps linearly, so this wrapper drives it in exponent
space and synchronizes ``base ** exponent`` as the value. Everything else,
including ``continuous_update``, behaves like :class:`Slider`.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name          | Type         | Description                                                       | Default    |
|---------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| value         | int \| float | Synchronized component value on the real scale, not the exponent. | `1`        |
| label         | str          | Visible or accessible label for the component.                    | `''`       |
| base          | int \| float | Logarithm base.                                                   | `10`       |
| min_exponent  | int \| float | Smallest exponent the slider can reach.                           | `0`        |
| max_exponent  | int \| float | Largest exponent the slider can reach.                            | `4`        |
| step          | int \| float | Exponent step between slider positions.                           | `0.1`      |
| disabled      | bool         | Whether the component should render disabled.                     | `False`    |
| value_display | str \| None  | Tooltip, text, or hidden value presentation.                      | `None`     |
| description   | str \| None  | Helper text displayed with the input.                             | `None`     |
| **props       | Any          | JSON-safe Slider props forwarded to Astryx.                       | `{}`       |
| See           |              |                                                                   | _required_ |
